result: PI3Kβ prioritizes interactions with membrane-tethered phosphotyrosine (pY) peptides over Rac1(GTP) or Gβγ alone. Single-molecule TIRF microscopy showed that only pY peptides robustly localized PI3Kβ to supported membranes, while Rac1(GTP) or Gβγ alone showed minimal or 2000-fold reduced binding frequency. This prioritization was consistent across various lipid compositions.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. Reviewer 2 states 'the primary regulator of PI3Kβ are tyrosine phosphorylated peptides' and that 'other activators...have relatively weak impacts on their own.' Reviewer 3 emphasizes this as 'one of the most profoundly novel activation mechanisms' and notes that 'Gβγ heterodimers and Rac1 alone have almost no ability to recruit PI3Kβ to the membranes.'

result: Membrane-tethered pY peptides strongly localize PI3Kβ to membranes but provide only modest stimulation of lipid kinase activity. Membrane-conjugated pY increased PI(3,4,5)P3 production 207-fold compared to solution pY, yet the calculated kcat was only 3 PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids/s•PI3Kβ for the pY-PI3Kβ complex.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly validates this finding, stating 'the current manuscript shows that the effect of membrane-conjugated peptides on the enzyme activity is profound, in terms of recruiting the enzyme to membranes' while noting the distinction between recruitment and catalytic activation. Reviewer 2 acknowledges the 'precision and clarity of mechanistic insight' provided by the reconstitution system.

result: PI3Kβ is synergistically activated by pY combined with either Gβγ or Rac1(GTP) through allosteric regulation rather than enhanced membrane recruitment alone. The PI3Kβ-pY-Gβγ complex showed only ~2-fold increased membrane localization but a 22-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat = 57 PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids/s•PI3Kβ), indicating allosteric modulation of enzyme activity.
evaluation: All reviewers strongly support this central finding. Reviewer 3 states 'the authors also show that this increased recruitment to membranes accounts for relatively little increase in activity, and that the far greater component of activation is due to an allosteric effect.' Reviewer 1 calls this 'compelling results concerning the mechanism of their activation.' The distinction between recruitment and allosteric activation is identified as a key advance.

result: Following pY engagement, PI3Kβ can associate with Gβγ, requiring nSH2 domain displacement from the Gβγ binding site. AlphaFold modeling and mutant analysis showed that the nSH2 domain sterically blocks Gβγ binding to p110β, and the nSH2(R358A) mutant unable to bind pY could not engage Gβγ. This resulted in 2-fold increased membrane localization and 1.9-fold increased dwell time.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly endorses this mechanism: 'The proposal for competition between Gbg binding and the nSH2 is consistent with the behavior of an nSH2 mutant that cannot bind to pY and which, consequently, does not vacate the Gbg-binding site.' The reviewer also notes the structural model is 'consistent with HDX-MS analyses that were published previously,' though acknowledging 'there is no experimental structure to support this structural model.'

result: Active Rac1(GTP) synergistically enhances PI3Kβ activity when combined with pY. Membranes with pY-Rac1(GTP) showed 1.4-fold enhanced localization, 1.5-fold increased dwell time, and 28% decreased displacement compared to pY-Rac1(GDP). After accounting for localization differences, a 4.3-fold increase in catalytic activity (kcat = 13 PI(3,4,5)P3 lipids/sec) was calculated.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 acknowledges the study demonstrates 'how PI3Kβ is uniquely activated by phosphorylated tyrosine kinase receptors, Gbeta/gamma heterodimers and the small G protein Rac1.' The quantitative kinetic measurements for Rac1 are treated as part of the comprehensive mechanistic characterization that all reviewers praise.

result: PI3Kβ cooperatively binds to one doubly phosphorylated PDGFR-derived peptide through both nSH2 and cSH2 domains. Single-molecule analysis showed that nSH2(R358A) and cSH2(R649A) mutants had 60-75% reduced membrane localization and reduced affinity, but maintained diffusion coefficients indistinguishable from wild-type, consistent with binding to a single peptide.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 emphasizes the 'beautiful, high quality, well controlled and internally consistent' results. The single-molecule diffusion analysis supporting cooperative binding is part of the methodological rigor that reviewers consistently praise, with no concerns raised about these specific findings.

result: Gβγ alone can subtly stimulate PI3Kβ lipid kinase activity without strongly enhancing membrane localization. The PI3Kβ(K532D,K533D) mutant unable to interact with Gβγ was insensitive to Gβγ-mediated activation, confirming the requirement for direct interaction.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes this observation is 'similar to previous observations' and is consistent with the overall finding that Gβγ alone has minimal recruitment capability. The mutant control experiment is part of the well-controlled experimental design that reviewers consistently validate.

result: Maximum synergistic activation by Gβγ occurred at membrane densities greater than 2400 molecules/μm². Varying Gβγ density showed a threshold requirement for full synergistic activation.
evaluation: This quantitative parameter is part of the comprehensive kinetic characterization. Reviewer 2 notes the 'precision and clarity of mechanistic insight' enabled by the reconstitution system, which includes these density-dependent measurements. No concerns were raised about this finding.

result: This is the first study to reconstitute membrane localization and activation of a class 1A PI3K using multiple signaling inputs that are all membrane-tethered in a physiologically relevant configuration, addressing a gap where previous studies used solution-based peptides.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the study 'will be a landmark contribution to the signaling field' and emphasizes 'the particular strengths of the work arise to a great extend from the reconstitution system better mimicking the natural environment of the plasma membrane than previous setups have.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the current manuscript shows that the effect of membrane-conjugated peptides on the enzyme activity is profound' and that 'these observations...would not have been possible with bulk measurements.'

result: Previous studies in neutrophils and in vitro biochemistry suggested PI3Kβ is synergistically activated through coincidence detection of RTKs and Gβγ, with robust activation requiring coincident RTK and GPCR pathway activation and depending most strongly on Gβγ binding.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes the current results 'reverse an impression that had built in large parts of the broader signalling and PI3K communities that all of the inputs to PI3Kβ were relatively equivalent, however, these conclusions were based on "in cell" or in vivo studies that were very difficult to interpret clearly.' This validates the prior cellular observations while clarifying their mechanistic basis.
